s: Under Article 153 of the Constitution, which of the following is permissible?
o: A single Governor may be appointed for two or more States
A State may function without a Governor for an indefinite period
Only Union Territories can have a common Governor
A Governor may be elected jointly by two State Legislatures
x: Article 153 provides for a Governor for each State, while the Seventh Amendment Act, 1956 enables one person to serve as Governor of two or more States.

s: Until when does a Governor continue in office after completing his normal term of five years?
o: The State Legislature passes a resolution
The next general election to the Assembly
x: The normal term is five years, but the Governor continues in office until the successor enters office.

s: Who determines the emoluments of a Governor?
x: Under Article 158, a Governor's emoluments are fixed by Parliament by law, not by the State Legislature.

s: By convention, before a Governor is appointed, who is consulted?
o: The Chief Minister of the State
The Chief Justice of the High Court
x: By convention the Governor is generally an outsider and the State's Chief Minister is consulted; the Constitution does not mandate this.

s: Which Article of the Constitution lays down the qualifications of a Governor?
x: Article 157 deals with qualifications; 155 with appointment, 156 with tenure and 158 with conditions of office.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Governor's immunity under Article 361?
o: The Governor is not answerable to any court for official acts
The Governor cannot be arrested or imprisoned during the term of office
Civil proceedings concerning personal acts require two months' notice
Criminal proceedings can be instituted during the term with prior permission of the High Court
x: No criminal proceedings can be instituted against the Governor during the term, even with a court's prior permission.

s: Who is the real executive head of a State?
o: The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly
x: The Chief Minister is the real executive head and heads the Council of Ministers; the Governor is the nominal or constitutional head.

s: Which of the following statements regarding the qualifications of the Governor is incorrect?
o: The person must have completed 35 years of age.
The person must be a citizen of India.
The person should not hold any office of profit.
The person may continue as a member of Parliament after becoming Governor.
x: Option D is incorrect: a Governor cannot be a member of Parliament or a State Legislature, and must give up any such seat on appointment. They must be a citizen, at least 35, and hold no office of profit.

s: Who administers the oath of office to the Governor of a State?
o: Chief Justice of the concerned High Court
x: Under Article 159, the Governor's oath is administered by the Chief Justice of the concerned High Court.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 154 – Executive power of the State vested in the Governor
x: Article 154 vests the executive power of the State in the Governor. Article 153 provides a Governor for each State, 159 the oath, and 213 ordinances.

s: What did the Supreme Court hold in B.P. Singhal v. Union of India (2010)?
o: the Governor's office is completely independent of the President's pleasure
a Governor cannot be removed arbitrarily or merely because the Centre's Government has changed
a Governor can be removed only after impeachment by Parliament
a Governor can be removed whenever the Union Government changes
x: The pleasure doctrine is not unfettered: removal cannot be arbitrary or based merely on a change in the Government at the Centre. Such removal is open to limited judicial review.

s: To whom does a Governor address his resignation?
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
x: A Governor resigns to the President; he may also be transferred and reappointed.

s: During whose pleasure does a Governor hold office?
x: Article 156 incorporates the President's pleasure, though B.P. Singhal held it cannot be exercised arbitrarily.

s: To which of the following bodies is the Governor constitutionally answerable in the ordinary discharge of the office?
o: The Council of Ministers of the State alone
x: The Governor is not answerable to either House of Parliament, to the State Legislature, or to the State Council of Ministers.

s: On which fund are the emoluments of a Governor charged?
x: Under Article 202(3), the Governor's emoluments are charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment Act made it possible to appoint the same person as Governor of two or more States?
x: The 7th Amendment, 1956 added a proviso to Article 153 so that one person can be Governor of two or more States.

s: Which Article of the Constitution makes the Governor an integral part of the State Legislature?
x: Article 168 says the State Legislature consists of the Governor and the House or Houses; he is part of it without being a member.

s: Which of the following correctly identifies an Andhra Pradesh-specific Article 356-related reference?
o: President’s Rule in 1984 during the Telugu Desam Party formation and a 2019 Supreme Court dissolution
President’s Rule in 1992 following the dissolution of the Tamil Nadu Assembly
President’s Rule in 1973 during the Jai Andhra movement and the 2020 High Court ‘breakdown’ episode
Governor’s Rule in 1973 under Section 92 of the J&K Constitution
x: The Andhra Pradesh references are President’s Rule in 1973 during the Jai Andhra movement and the 2020 Andhra Pradesh High Court episode concerning constitutional breakdown.

s: What was the head of State of Jammu and Kashmir called until 1965?
x: The head of State of Jammu and Kashmir was called Sadr-e-Riyasat until 1965, when the title became Governor.

s: Under Section 8 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, the Governor was given special responsibility mainly in relation to which area?
o: Law and order and allocation of government buildings in Hyderabad
Conduct of elections to all local bodies in both States
Appointment of judges to the Telangana High Court
x: Section 8 assigned special responsibility to the Governor for law and order and allocation of government buildings, mainly in Hyderabad as the common capital.

s: The special responsibility assigned to the Governor under Section 8 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 ceased with the expiry of the common-capital period on:
x: The ten-year common-capital period ended on 2 June 2024, after which the special responsibility under Section 8 lapsed.

s: When was President's Rule first imposed in the Telugu region, in Andhra State?
x: Andhra State came under President's Rule in 1954-55. 1951 is the first-ever instance (Punjab); 1973 was the Jai Andhra spell in Andhra Pradesh; 1984 was the Nadendla Bhaskara Rao episode, not President's Rule.

s: Who became Governor of Andhra Pradesh in February 2023?
x: S. Abdul Nazeer has been Governor of Andhra Pradesh since February 2023.

s: Who was the first Governor of Andhra State (1953) and of Andhra Pradesh (1956)?
x: C.M. Trivedi was the first Governor of both Andhra State (1953) and Andhra Pradesh (1956). E.S.L. Narasimhan was the common Governor of AP and Telangana (2014-19); Neelam Sanjiva Reddy was the first CM and K.V. Ranga Reddy the Deputy CM of united AP.

s: How many Deputy Chief Ministers did the 2019-24 Andhra Pradesh government have?
x: The 2019-24 Andhra Pradesh government had five Deputy CMs; the Deputy CM is not a constitutional post.

s: Who was the common Governor of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana during the period 2014 to July 2019?
x: E.S.L. Narasimhan served as the common Governor of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana from 2014 to July 2019.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Sarojini Naidu was the first woman Governor of Uttar Pradesh.
Padmaja Naidu was the first woman Governor of West Bengal.
Sarojini Naidu was the first woman Governor of West Bengal.
Padmaja Naidu was the daughter of Sarojini Naidu.
x: Option C is incorrect: Sarojini Naidu, India's first woman Governor, governed Uttar Pradesh. Her daughter Padmaja Naidu was the first woman Governor of West Bengal.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about President's Rule in the Telugu region?
o: The 1984 Nadendla episode was a spell of President's Rule
Andhra State was under it in 1954-55
Andhra Pradesh first came under it in 1973 (Jai Andhra)
Undivided Andhra Pradesh was under it twice as of 2004
x: The 1984 Nadendla episode was not President's Rule; Andhra Pradesh's first spell was in 1973.

s: Who has been the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh since June 2024?
x: N. Chandrababu Naidu became CM in June 2024; S. Abdul Nazeer is the Governor and K. Pawan Kalyan the Deputy CM.

s: Who was the first Governor of West Bengal?
x: C. Rajagopalachari was the first Governor of West Bengal; Padmaja Naidu was its first woman Governor.

s: Who was the Governor of Andhra Pradesh from 2019 to 2023?
x: Biswabhusan Harichandan succeeded E.S.L. Narasimhan in 2019 and served till 2023, when S. Abdul Nazeer took over.

s: Under Article 174, what is the maximum gap allowed between two sessions of a State Legislature?
x: Article 174 bars a gap of more than six months between two sessions.

s: Under which Article does the Governor have the power to pardon offences against State laws?
x: The Governor pardons under Article 161 (State laws only); the President under Article 72 (all cases).

s: Under which Article does the Governor deliver a special address at the first session after each general election and at the first session of each year?
x: The special address under Article 176 is mandatory on both occasions and is delivered on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers.

s: The Governor nominates what proportion of the members of the Legislative Council?
x: Under Article 171, the Governor nominates one-sixth of the members of a State Legislative Council from persons having special knowledge or practical experience in specified fields.

s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Appointment of the State PSC Chairman and members – Article 316
All executive action of the State Government – Article 165
Appointment of the Chief Minister and Ministers – Article 164
x: Executive action in the Governor's name is under Article 166; Article 165 concerns the Advocate-General.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Governor's power to recommend President's Rule — Article 360
x: The Governor's report recommending President's Rule is associated with Article 356, not Article 360. Articles 243K, 243I and 213 are correctly matched.

s: In January 2026, Governors in Opposition-ruled States drew controversy by walking out of or skipping the mandatory address under which Article?
x: The controversy concerned the mandatory Governor's address under Article 176; under Nabam Rebia, the address must reflect Cabinet policy.

s: Of which institutions is the Governor of a State the Chancellor?
o: the State universities, as provided by the applicable university laws
all Central universities located in that State
x: The Governor is also the Chancellor of State universities under the applicable State university laws. This role does not extend to all Central or private universities.

s: Which one of the following can the Governor of a State NOT do?
o: Appoint the Chairman of the State Public Service Commission
Remove a member of the State Public Service Commission
x: Although the Governor appoints SPSC members, only the President can remove them. The Governor does appoint the Advocate-General (Art. 165), the SPSC Chairman (Art. 316) and the State Election Commissioner (Art. 243K).

s: The Governor appoints District Judges in consultation with which of the following?
x: Under Article 233, the Governor appoints district judges in consultation with the High Court.

s: Who places the CAG's report relating to a State before the State Legislature?
x: The Governor places the CAG report on the State, along with the State PSC and State Finance Commission reports, before the Legislature.

s: To matters in which Lists does the President's ordinance-making power extend?
o: State List and the Concurrent List
Union List and the Concurrent List
x: The President's ordinance power is co-extensive with Parliament's legislative power, including the Concurrent List.

s: Who may withdraw an ordinance, and when?
o: Only Parliament may withdraw it after six weeks.
Only the State Legislature may withdraw it.
Neither the President nor the Governor may withdraw it once issued.
The President or Governor may withdraw it at any time, as applicable.
x: The President or the Governor can withdraw their ordinance at any time (Article 123(2)(b) / 213(2)(b)).

s: In which of the following circumstances does the Governor require instructions from the President before promulgating an ordinance?
o: Whenever the State Legislature has two Houses
When a Bill containing the same provisions would require the President's prior sanction or would have to be reserved for his consideration
Whenever the ordinance concerns any State List subject
Whenever the ordinance concerns any Concurrent List subject
x: The Governor requires the President's instructions where a Bill containing the same provisions would require prior sanction of the President or would have to be reserved for his consideration.

s: Which of the following is NOT appointed by the Governor of a State?
o: The Chairman of the State Public Service Commission
x: The President, not the Governor, appoints High Court judges; the Governor appoints the Advocate-General (165), SPSC members (316) and the State Election Commissioner (243K).

s: The President's pardoning power under Article 72, unlike the Governor's under Article 161, extends to:
o: Offences against Concurrent List laws only
Cases decided by a High Court only
x: Article 72 covers all cases, while the Governor's power under Article 161 is limited to offences against State laws.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 243K – Appointment of the State Election Commissioner
Article 233 – Appointment of High Court judges
x: Article 243K is correct. Article 176 (not 175) is the mandatory address, Article 192 excludes anti-defection, and Article 233 covers District Judges.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: A President’s ordinance must be approved by Parliament.
A Governor’s ordinance must be approved by the President.
Approval of a Governor’s ordinance is not given by the Union Council of Ministers.
A Governor’s ordinance must be approved by the State Legislature.
x: B is incorrect: a Governor's ordinance must be approved by the State Legislature, not by the President (though some need prior Presidential instructions). A President's ordinance needs Parliament's approval.

s: The Chairman of a State Public Service Commission is appointed by the Governor; who alone can remove him?
x: The Governor appoints SPSC members under Article 316, but only the President can remove them.

s: On whose opinion does the Governor decide whether a member of the State Legislature has become disqualified under Article 192?
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
x: Under Article 192 the Governor decides non-defection disqualification, but he must act on the opinion of the Election Commission.

s: Under which Article of the Constitution does the Governor summon, prorogue and dissolve the State Legislative Assembly?
x: Article 174 lets the Governor summon and prorogue the Houses and dissolve the Assembly; 175-176 deal with addresses, 213 with ordinances.

s: When does an ordinance promulgated by the Governor cease to operate if it is not approved?
o: Three months after the State Legislature reassembles
At the end of the financial year
Six weeks after the State Legislature reassembles
Six months after it is promulgated
x: A Governor's ordinance under Article 213 lapses six weeks after the State Legislature reassembles, unless disapproved earlier.

s: Which Article provides for the State Council of Ministers aiding and advising the Governor?
x: Article 163 provides for a State Council of Ministers to aid and advise the Governor, like Article 74 for the President. Article 164 deals with appointment of Ministers.

s: How does the constitutional discretion of the Governor compare with that of the President?
x: The Governor's discretion is wider than the President's; the Constitution confers no comparable general discretion on the President.

s: If a Chief Minister loses majority in the Legislative Assembly, he:
o: Continues in office until the next general election
Can be removed only by impeachment
Must resign or may be dismissed
x: A Chief Minister who loses majority must resign or may be dismissed; once a new Chief Minister is sworn in, the former ceases to hold office.

s: In May 2026, after Mamata Banerjee refused to resign despite losing the election, which provision was cited as allowing the Governor to dismiss a Chief Minister who has lost majority?
x: Ministers hold office during the Governor's pleasure under Article 164, which allows dismissal of a CM who has lost majority. Article 356 is President's Rule, Article 163(3) bars inquiry into ministerial advice, and Article 361 grants the Governor immunity.

s: Which of the following is a constitutional or express discretionary power of the Governor?
o: Dissolving the Assembly after a ministry loses its majority
Dismissing a ministry that has lost its majority
Reserving a Bill for the consideration of the President
Appointing a Chief Minister in a hung Assembly
x: Reserving a Bill for the President under Article 200 is an express constitutional discretion. The other options describe situational discretion.

s:
Assertion (A): The Governor can reserve a Bill for the President even when the Council of Ministers advises otherwise.
Reason (R): The Governor is not bound by the advice of the Council of Ministers in all matters.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true: the Governor can reserve a bill for the President against ministerial advice because the Governor is not bound by that advice in every matter. R explains A.

s: Which one of the following is associated with the Tamil Nadu Kurian Joseph Committee of 2026?
o: A proposal to replace Governors with elected Chief Ministers
A proposal for a new Schedule codifying the Governor’s discretion
A proposal to transfer all State finances to local bodies
x: The Kurian Joseph Committee was reported to have proposed a new Schedule to codify the Governor’s discretion.

s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Seeking information from the Chief Minister – Article 239
Reserving a Bill for the President – Article 200
Administration of an adjoining Union Territory – Article 239
x: The Governor seeks information from the Chief Minister under Article 167; Article 239 concerns administration of Union Territories.

s: Under Article 163(2), what is the status of the Governor's decision on whether a matter falls within his discretion?
o: Subject to approval by the Council of Ministers
Subject to approval by the President
Final, but not completely immune from judicial review
x: Article 163(2) makes the Governor's decision final on whether a matter is discretionary, but it does not create complete immunity from judicial review.

s: Under Article 163(1) of the Constitution, the Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister aids and advises the Governor
o: Except in matters where the Governor is required to act in his discretion
Only when the Legislative Assembly is in session
x: Article 163(1) provides for aid and advice by the Council of Ministers except where the Governor is required to exercise discretion.

s: Which provision bars courts from inquiring into the advice tendered by Ministers to the Governor?
x: Article 163(3) bars courts from inquiring into ministers' advice; Article 163(2) makes the Governor's decision on discretion final.

s: Under which Article is the Governor given special responsibility for law and order in Arunachal Pradesh?
x: Article 371H gives the Governor of Arunachal Pradesh law and order responsibility; Article 371A does so for Nagaland.

s: In a hung State Assembly, the Sarkaria and Punchhi approach gives first preference for forming the government to:
o: A post-poll alliance with outside support
x: The order is pre-poll alliance, largest party with support, post-poll coalition, then post-poll alliance with outside support.

s: In the Tamil Nadu 2026 hung Assembly situation, the Governor invited C. Joseph Vijay after receiving letters of support from 120 members, following which convention?
o: Appointment of the leader of the single largest party without a floor test
Appointment by the President under Article 356
Selection by the Legislative Council under Article 169
The Sarkaria-Punchhi order, followed by an early floor test
x: The Governor invited C. Joseph Vijay on the basis of 120 letters of support, following the Sarkaria-Punchhi order and requiring an early floor test.

s: Under which Article does the Governor act as administrator of an adjoining Union Territory?
x: Under Article 239(2), a Governor appointed administrator of an adjoining UT acts independently of his State Council of Ministers.

s: Who among the following reports to the President on the administration of the Scheduled Areas in a State under the Fifth Schedule?
o: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
x: Under the Fifth Schedule the Governor reports to the President on the administration of Scheduled Areas in the State.

s:
Consider the following statements about Article 163:
1. No court can inquire into the advice tendered by Ministers to the Governor.
2. The Governor's decision on whether a matter is within his discretion is final.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Article 163(3) bars courts from inquiring into ministerial advice, and Article 163(2) makes the Governor's decision on his discretion final.

s: Under which Article of the Constitution does the Governor of Nagaland have special responsibility for law and order?
x: Article 371A gives the Governor of Nagaland special responsibility for law and order; 371H does the same for Arunachal Pradesh.

s: Under the Fifth Schedule, the Governor makes regulations for the peace and good government of a Scheduled Area after consulting which body?
x: Under paragraph 5 of the Fifth Schedule the Governor may make such regulations, but only after consulting the Tribes Advisory Council where one exists.

s: What is the maximum number of members of a Tribes Advisory Council under the Fifth Schedule?
x: A Tribes Advisory Council has not more than twenty members, about three-fourths of whom are ST members of the State Legislative Assembly.

s: Which case rejected the dissolution of an Assembly based on unproven fears of horse-trading?
x: Rameshwar Prasad (2006) rejected dissolution on unproven fears of horse-trading.

s: In S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994), the dismissal of the Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Himachal Pradesh governments was upheld on which ground?
o: Loss of majority on the floor
x: The nine-judge bench in S.R. Bommai held secularism to be a basic feature and upheld those dismissals on that ground.

s: How many judges decided the S.R. Bommai case (1994) on Article 356?
x: S.R. Bommai was decided by a nine-judge bench; Shamsher Singh (1974) had seven judges.

s: Which of the following is a proper ground for invoking Article 356?
o: An intra-party dispute in the ruling party
An ordinary law and order problem
x: Flagrant defiance of constitutional directions is a proper ground; intra-party disputes, maladministration alone and ordinary law and order are improper.

s: What may happen to the State Legislative Assembly during President's Rule?
x: During President's Rule the Assembly may be suspended or dissolved, while Parliament legislates for the State.

s: Parliamentary legislation for a State under President's Rule is enabled by which Article?
x: Article 357 provides for the exercise of legislative powers under a proclamation issued under Article 356.

s: What did the Supreme Court hold in S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994) about a proclamation under Article 356?
o: reviewable only after approval by the State Legislature
subject to judicial review, and the Union must disclose relevant material
beyond judicial review in all circumstances
reviewable only by the Governor of the concerned State
x: The nine-judge Bench in S.R. Bommai held that an Article 356 proclamation is subject to judicial review and that the Centre must show relevant material supporting it.

s: According to S.R. Bommai, where must the majority support of a State ministry ordinarily be tested?
o: On the floor of the Legislative Assembly
In Raj Bhavan by the Governor
Through a report of the State Election Commission
x: S.R. Bommai held that majority must ordinarily be tested on the floor of the House, not in Raj Bhavan.

s: After the Ayodhya events of December 1992, the BJP governments of Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and which other State were dismissed?
x: The BJP governments of UP, MP, Rajasthan and Himachal Pradesh were removed; Bommai upheld the dismissals of MP, Rajasthan and HP.

s: What is the maximum period for which President's Rule can ordinarily continue?
x: President's Rule continues six months at a time with parliamentary approval, up to a maximum of three years.

s: To extend President's Rule beyond one year, a National Emergency must be in operation and which body must certify that elections cannot be held?
x: Beyond one year, a National Emergency must be in force and the Election Commission must certify that elections cannot be held.

s: In which State was President's Rule under Article 356 first imposed in 1951?
x: President's Rule was first imposed in Punjab in 1951; Kerala (1959) saw the first dismissal of an elected government.

s: On which date did the latest spell of President's Rule in Manipur begin?
x: The latest spell began on 13 February 2025 (Manipur's 11th) and was revoked on 4 February 2026.

s: Under the former Constitution of Jammu and Kashmir, for how long at most could Governor's Rule continue?
o: 6 months under Section 92 of the J&K Constitution
x: In the former Jammu and Kashmir constitutional arrangement, Governor’s Rule was imposed under Section 92 of the J&K Constitution for six months, after which Article 356 could apply.

s: Which case held that an Assembly should not be dissolved before Parliament approves a proclamation under Article 356?
x: Bommai protected the Assembly pending parliamentary approval, allowed restoration of a displaced ministry and treated secularism as a basic feature.

s: On what basis may the President impose President's Rule in a State under Article 356?
o: Only on the report of the Governor
Only on a resolution of the State Legislative Assembly
Only on the advice of the Chief Minister
On the report of the Governor or otherwise
x: Under Article 356 the President acts on the Governor's report or otherwise when the State cannot be governed according to the Constitution.

s: Where and when did the first dismissal of an elected State government under Article 356 take place?
x: President's Rule was first imposed in Punjab in 1951, but the first elected government dismissed was Kerala's in 1959.

s: Which of the following States has never been under President's Rule?
x: Telangana and Chhattisgarh have never been under President's Rule; Manipur has had it most often.

s: What happened to the Andhra Pradesh High Court's 2020 observation of a 'constitutional breakdown' in the State?
x: The AP High Court's 2020 'constitutional breakdown' observation was stayed by the Supreme Court.

s: In which State has President's Rule been imposed the most number of times?
x: Manipur has been under President's Rule more often than any other State; its 11th spell began on 13 February 2025.

s: Under which Article of the Constitution can President's Rule be imposed when a State fails to comply with the directions of the Union?
x: Article 365 treats failure to follow Union directions as a situation in which the State's government cannot be carried on per the Constitution, so Article 356 may be used.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. President's Rule may be imposed on the report of the Governor or otherwise.
2. Failure of a State to comply with Union directions is a ground for President's Rule under Article 365.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Article 356 acts on the Governor's report or otherwise, and Article 365 adds failure to follow Union directions as a ground.

s: Reservation by the Governor for the President is mandatory for a Bill that:
o: Derogates from the powers of the High Court
x: A Bill derogating from the High Court's powers must be reserved; not every Bill affecting State finances needs mandatory reservation.

s: Under which Article does a State Bill imposing restrictions on inter-State trade require the previous sanction of the President before introduction?
x: Article 304(b) requires previous Presidential sanction before a Bill restricting inter-State trade is introduced. Article 288 concerns taxes on water/electricity in inter-State river projects, Article 254(2) Concurrent List repugnancy, and Article 31C property-related protection.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about a State Bill reserved for the President under Article 201?
o: A returned Bill must be reconsidered by the State Legislature within six months
Article 201 prescribes no fixed time limit for the President's decision
The President is not bound to assent even after the Bill is passed again
The President may direct the Governor to return even a Money Bill for reconsideration
x: Only a non-Money Bill can be returned to the State Legislature for reconsideration.

s: Under Article 200 of the Constitution, which one of the following is NOT an option available to the Governor in respect of a Bill passed by the State Legislature?
o: To withhold assent to the Bill
To reserve the Bill for the consideration of the President
To return a Money Bill for reconsideration
x: The Governor may return a Bill for reconsideration only if it is not a Money Bill. The other three are options available under Article 200.

s: If a Bill returned by the Governor is passed again by the State Legislature, the Governor:
o: Must reserve it for the President
x: If the Legislature re-passes a Bill returned for reconsideration, the Governor must assent and cannot withhold assent again.

s: A Bill once reserved for the consideration of the President may be reserved again after re-enactment only when it has been:
o: Approved by the State Cabinet unanimously
x: A Bill may be reserved only once. A re-enacted Bill cannot ordinarily be reserved again unless it has been materially altered.

s: In State of Tamil Nadu v. Governor of Tamil Nadu (April 2025), the Supreme Court held that the referral of ten re-enacted Bills to the President was:
o: Valid because the Governor has absolute discretion under Article 200
Invalid only because the Bills were Money Bills
Unconstitutional, and the Court declared the Bills assented to by invoking Article 142
Valid because a re-enacted Bill must always be reserved for the President
x: The Supreme Court held that the referral of the ten re-enacted Bills was unconstitutional and used Article 142 to declare them assented to.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Article 201?
o: Even after reconsideration, the President is not bound to assent
The President may direct the Governor to return a non-Money Bill for reconsideration
The President may withhold assent to a Bill reserved by the Governor
The Constitution fixes a period within which the President must decide every reserved Bill
x: Article 201 prescribes no fixed time limit for the President's decision on a reserved Bill.

s: Under which Article is a State Bill on taxes on water or electricity in inter-State river projects reserved for the President?
x: Taxes on water/electricity in inter-State river projects fall under Article 288; Article 304(b) concerns restrictions on inter-State trade.

s: Which Article deals with Bills reserved by the Governor for the consideration of the President?
x: Article 201 deals with Bills reserved for the President; Article 200 covers the Governor's choices on a State Bill.

s: The reservation of State Bills for the consideration of the President is an example of which of the following?
x: Reservation of Bills by the Governor for the President is a classic example of central control over the States.

s: Which of the following statements regarding the Governor's action on State Bills is incorrect?
o: The Governor must return an ordinary Bill within a fixed time limit.
The Governor may return an ordinary Bill for reconsideration.
The Governor may give assent to a State Bill.
The Governor may withhold assent to a State Bill.
x: Option A is incorrect: the Governor may return an ordinary bill, but the Constitution sets no time limit for acting on it. The Governor can also assent or withhold assent.

s: Under which Article of the Constitution is a State law on a Concurrent List subject that is repugnant to a Central law reserved for the President's assent so that it may prevail in the State?
x: Under Article 254(2) a repugnant State law on a Concurrent List subject prevails in the State only if reserved for and assented to by the President.

s: The Supreme Court's decision in State of Punjab v. Principal Secretary to Governor (2023) held that the Governor:
o: Could reserve every State Bill for the President without giving reasons
Could keep Bills pending indefinitely if no time limit was expressly stated
Must act as soon as possible and cannot keep Bills pending indefinitely
Could reject a Bill permanently after returning it once
x: The 2023 Punjab case held that the Governor must act as soon as possible and cannot keep Bills pending indefinitely. It also affirmed the consequence of re-passage of a returned Bill.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the November 2025 Presidential Reference opinion?
o: The President need not seek the Supreme Court's advice on each reserved Bill
Judicial review is limited to issues such as mala fides and procedure
Courts may impose a fixed deadline for every Bill pending before a Governor
x: The opinion rejected court-imposed timelines, permitting only limited intervention in cases of prolonged unexplained inaction.

s: In the context of the 16th Presidential Reference, the Governor was described as the:
o: Permanent representative of the Union Cabinet in the State
Final constitutional sovereign of the State
Judicial guardian of the State Legislature
Guide, philosopher and friend of the government
x: The November 2025 Presidential Reference opinion described the Governor as a “guide, philosopher and friend” of the government.

s: Which decision prescribed timelines for the Governor and recognised deemed assent to State Bills?
o: State of Punjab v. Principal Secretary to Governor (2023)
State of Tamil Nadu v. Governor of Tamil Nadu (8 April 2025)
x: The 8 April 2025 ruling prescribed timelines and recognised deemed assent; the November 2025 Reference opinion rejected rigid deadlines and deemed assent.

s: In State of Tamil Nadu v. Governor of Tamil Nadu, decided on 8 April 2025, which timeline was associated with the Governor's action on Bills?
o: Two months, three months and two months on re-passage
Three months, six months and three months on re-passage
One month, three months and one month on re-passage
One month, six months and one month on re-passage
x: The ruling referred to timelines of one month, three months and one month on re-passage, along with the concept of deemed assent.

s: According to the November 2025 opinion in the 16th Presidential Reference, the Governor, while choosing among the options under Article 200, is:
o: Required to refer every Bill to the Supreme Court
Bound in every case by the advice of the State Council of Ministers
Not bound by such advice in choosing among the Article 200 options
Required to follow the advice of the President alone
x: The Presidential Reference opinion stated that the Governor is not bound by the advice of the State Council of Ministers while choosing among the options available under Article 200.

s: Under which Article did the Supreme Court grant deemed assent to ten Tamil Nadu Bills in April 2025?
x: The 8 April 2025 ruling used Article 142 to grant deemed assent; the Article 143 Reference of November 2025 rejected deemed assent.

s: Rameshwar Prasad referred to the Sarkaria Commission in connection with which issue?
o: Misuse of reports under Article 356 and a cooling-off period before politicians become Governors
The procedure for electing the Governor
The Governor's power to appoint judges of the High Court
The distribution of royalty under the Sixth Schedule
x: Rameshwar Prasad cited Sarkaria regarding misuse of Article 356 reports and urged a cooling-off period before politicians are appointed as Governors.

s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that summoning, proroguing and dissolving the Assembly under Article 174 are not discretionary powers of the Governor?
x: Nabam Rebia held these powers and the address under Articles 175–176 are exercised on aid and advice, rejecting a general discretion.

s: Which judgment reaffirmed that the Governor is bound by Cabinet advice regarding pardon or remission under Article 161?
x: The Perarivalan judgment of 2022 held that the Governor is bound by Cabinet advice on pardon or remission under Article 161; this position was reaffirmed subsequently.

s:
Arrange the following cases in chronological order:
A. Perarivalan
B. Shamsher Singh
C. Nabam Rebia
D. S.R. Bommai
x: The correct sequence is Shamsher Singh (1974), S.R. Bommai (1994), Nabam Rebia (2016) and Perarivalan (2022).

s: How did the Supreme Court describe a Governor's public criticism of Cabinet policy in Shamsher Singh (1974)?
x: The seven-judge bench held the Governor bound by aid and advice and called public criticism of Cabinet policy an unconstitutional faux pas.

s: According to the recommendations of the First Administrative Reforms Commission’s Centre-State study team, deployment of central armed forces in States could take place:
o: On the request of the States or otherwise
Only with the prior approval of the State Legislature
Only on the direction of the Inter-State Council
x: The study team recommended deployment of central armed forces in States on their request or otherwise.

s: How did the Sarkaria Commission recommend that Article 356 be used?
o: As the first response to political instability
x: Sarkaria recommended Article 356 only as a last resort, along with a mandatory floor test and a politically neutral outsider as Governor.

s: Under which Article did the First ARC study team on Centre-State relations recommend an Inter-State Council?
x: The study team recommended an Inter-State Council under Article 263, along with non-partisan Governors, delegation of powers and more resources for States.

s: The Venkatachaliah Commission recommended that the Governor should be appointed by a committee consisting of:
o: The Prime Minister, Union Home Minister, Lok Sabha Speaker and the State Chief Minister
The President, Vice-President, Chief Justice of India and the State Chief Minister
The Prime Minister, Chief Justice of India, Governor and State Speaker
The Union Home Minister, Rajya Sabha Chairman, State Governor and Chief Minister
x: The recommended committee comprised the Prime Minister, Union Home Minister, Lok Sabha Speaker and the Chief Minister of the State concerned.

s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Punchhi Commission – Fixed tenure for the Governor
Sarkaria Commission – Politically neutral outsider as Governor and consultation with the CM
Rajamannar Committee – Review of Centre-State relations; recommendations not implemented
First ARC – Fixed tenure for the Governor
x: Fixed tenure for the Governor was the Punchhi Commission's recommendation; the First ARC stressed long public experience and a non-partisan attitude.

s: For how long did the Punchhi Commission recommend a localised emergency in a district?
x: Punchhi recommended a localised district emergency for up to three months, codification of Bommai guidelines and fixed tenure for Governors.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Punchhi Commission:
1. It recommended a fixed tenure for Governors.
2. It was set up in 2007 and reported in 2010.
3. It recommended that the Governor be appointed by a committee including the Lok Sabha Speaker.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Punchhi (2007-2010) recommended a fixed tenure; the appointment committee including the Lok Sabha Speaker was the NCRWC (Venkatachaliah) proposal.

s: What is the term of office of a Governor?
x: The Governor's term is five years, subject to the President's pleasure, and continues until a successor takes over.

s: Who was the first Chief Minister of united Andhra Pradesh (1956)?
x: Neelam Sanjeeva Reddy was the first CM of united Andhra Pradesh (1956-60). Tanguturi Prakasam was CM of Andhra State, Burgula Ramakrishna Rao of Hyderabad State, and N. Chandrababu Naidu the first CM of residuary AP (2014).

s: Who was the first Speaker of the Andhra State Legislative Assembly (1953)?
x: Nallapati Venkata Ramaiah was Speaker of the Andhra State Assembly (1953-55). Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao was the first Speaker of the united Andhra Pradesh Assembly (1956); Tanguturi Prakasam was the first Chief Minister of Andhra State.

s: Who was the first Chief Minister of Andhra State?
x: Tanguturi Prakasam became the first Chief Minister of Andhra State in 1953.

s: Who was the first Chief Minister of Hyderabad State?
x: Burgula Ramakrishna Rao was the first Chief Minister of Hyderabad State.

s: Who was the first Chief Minister of the residuary State of Andhra Pradesh after bifurcation in 2014?
x: N. Chandrababu Naidu became the first Chief Minister of residuary Andhra Pradesh in 2014.

s: Who was the first woman Chief Minister in India?
x: Sucheta Kripalani was the first woman Chief Minister; E.M.S. Namboodiripad was the first non-Congress Chief Minister.

s: Who was the first non-Congress Chief Minister in India?
x: E.M.S. Namboodiripad of Kerala was the first non-Congress Chief Minister.

s: In which year did Mayawati first become the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh?
x: Mayawati first became UP Chief Minister in 1995; by May 2002 she had become CM three times.

s: Who is the present Chief Minister of Maharashtra (2026)?
x: Devendra Fadnavis took oath as Maharashtra CM on 5 December 2024 for his third term and is in office in 2026.

s: A Chief Minister continues in office so long as he or she enjoys the confidence of which body?
x: The Chief Minister must retain the confidence of the Legislative Assembly. Loss of majority may lead to resignation or dismissal of the government after the position is established.

s: Under Article 164(2), to which body is the State Council of Ministers collectively responsible?
o: Both Houses of the State Legislature
x: Article 164(2) makes the Council of Ministers collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly alone. Ministers hold office at the Governor's pleasure but are not collectively responsible to him; the Council is not responsible to the Legislative Council.

s: What is the term of office of the Chief Minister?
x: The Constitution does not fix the Chief Minister's term.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 164(4) – Non-member may be a minister for twelve months
Article 164(5) – Salaries of ministers fixed by Parliament
Article 164(3) – Oath of ministers administered by the Governor
Article 164(2) – Collective responsibility to the Legislative Council
x: The Governor administers the oath under Art. 164(3). A non-member can be a minister for six months (164(4)), salaries are fixed by the State Legislature (164(5)), and responsibility is to the Assembly (164(2)).

s: In which of the following is the Chief Minister appointed by the President?
x: In States the Governor appoints the CM; in Delhi (Art. 239AA) and Puducherry the President appoints the CM.

s: Under which Article are the salaries of State ministers fixed by the State Legislature?
x: Article 164(5) leaves salaries to the State Legislature by law; until then the Second Schedule applies.

s: For how long can a person who is not a member of the State Legislature hold office as a Minister?
x: Under Article 164(4) a non-member Minister ceases to hold office after six consecutive months unless he becomes a member.

s: To whom does the Chief Minister of a State address his resignation?
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
x: The Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor under Article 164(1) and submits his resignation to the Governor.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about appointing a Chief Minister in a hung Assembly?
o: The Constitution lays down detailed criteria for the Governor's choice
The Governor may exercise discretion in selecting the Chief Minister
An early floor test is ordinarily used to establish majority support
A pre-poll alliance gets the first preference under Sarkaria and Punchhi
x: The Constitution gives no detailed criteria for a hung Assembly; the Governor uses discretion, followed by an early floor test.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Sarkaria and Punchhi order of preference for inviting a group to form the government in a hung Assembly?
o: A post-poll coalition comes before the single largest party with support
A post-poll alliance with outside support comes last
A pre-poll alliance gets first preference
The single largest party with support of others comes second
x: The order is pre-poll alliance, single largest party with support, post-poll coalition, then post-poll alliance with outside support.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 164(4) – Collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers
Article 164(2) – Collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers to the Assembly
x: Article 164(2) makes the State Council of Ministers collectively answerable to the Legislative Assembly; 164(3) is the oath and 164(5) the salaries.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the State Council of Ministers?
o: State Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the Chief Minister
A non-member may be a Minister but must become an MLA or MLC within six months
The Governor appoints the Chief Minister, normally the Assembly majority leader
Article 164 deals with the State Council of Ministers
x: State Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the Governor, not the Chief Minister.

s: If a no-confidence motion is passed in the State Legislative Assembly, who must resign?
o: The entire Council of Ministers, including the Chief Minister
x: The State ministry is collectively responsible to the Assembly (Art. 164(2)), so a passed no-confidence motion forces the whole ministry, CM included, to resign.

s: The Legislative Assembly of Andhra Pradesh has 175 seats. What is the maximum number of ministers, including the Chief Minister, that the State can have?
x: The stated maximum is 15 percent of the Assembly strength. Fifteen percent of 175 is 26.25, giving a maximum of 26 ministers when expressed as the applicable whole-number limit.

s: Which Amendment Act introduced the cap of 15% of the Assembly's strength on the size of a State Council of Ministers?
x: The 91st Amendment Act, 2003 (not 2001) fixed the 15% cap, including the CM, in Article 164(1A).

s: In which of the following groups of States is a Minister for Tribal Welfare compulsory under Article 164(1)?
o: Bihar, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha
Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha
Chhattisgarh, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha
x: The four States are Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha; Bihar was dropped in 2006.

s: By which Amendment was Bihar dropped from the list of States requiring a Tribal Welfare Minister?
x: The 94th Amendment, 2006 removed Bihar from the Article 164(1) list.

s: What is the minimum strength of a State Council of Ministers, including the Chief Minister?
x: The 91st Amendment (2003) caps a State ministry at 15% of the Assembly with a minimum of 12.

s: Under the 91st Amendment Act, 2003, a State Council of Ministers including the CM cannot exceed what share of the Assembly's total strength?
x: The ceiling is 15% of the Legislative Assembly's total strength, with a minimum of 12 (Art. 164(1A)).

s: In which of the following groups of States is the appointment of a Minister for Tribal Welfare mandatory?
o: Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha and West Bengal
Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha
Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Maharashtra and Odisha
Chhattisgarh, Bihar, Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh
x: A Minister for Tribal Welfare is mandatory in Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha. Bihar was removed from the list by the 94th Amendment Act, 2006.

s:
Consider the following statements comparing the State executive with the Union executive:
1. The Chief Minister mirrors the Prime Minister, whose Council of Ministers is covered by Articles 74 and 75.
2. The State has a constitutional counterpart of the Vice-President.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct: the CM is the State counterpart of the PM (Arts. 74-75). Statement 2 is wrong: a State has no counterpart of the Vice-President. Hence '1 only'.

s: Under Article 167, who is the chief link between the Governor and the State Council of Ministers?
x: Article 167 makes the Chief Minister the link, communicating Council decisions to the Governor and placing matters before the Council when required.

s: Seeking information from the Chief Minister under Article 167 is a constitutional discretion of whom?
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
x: Under Article 167, the Governor can call on the Chief Minister for information about administration and legislative proposals, and this is a constitutional discretion of the Governor. The CM is the chief link between the Governor and the Council of Ministers.

s: Which of the following is a constitutional duty of the Chief Minister under Article 167?
o: Reserving Bills for the consideration of the President
Communicating Cabinet decisions to the Governor
x: Under Article 167, the Chief Minister must communicate the decisions of the Council of Ministers to the Governor and furnish information the Governor seeks.

s: What is the constitutional status of the office of Deputy Chief Minister in a State?
o: A political arrangement not specifically mentioned in the Constitution
x: The Constitution does not specifically mention the office; the incumbent is sworn in as a minister and the post is a political arrangement.

s: Who was the Deputy Chief Minister of united Andhra Pradesh in 1956?
x: K.V. Ranga Reddy was Deputy CM of united AP in 1956, when Neelam Sanjeeva Reddy was CM.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Deputy Chief Minister?
o: The post is not mentioned in the Constitution
A Deputy CM is sworn in as a Minister
He ranks with Union Ministers of State in precedence
The post is created by Article 164(1A)
x: The Deputy CM is not mentioned in the Constitution; Article 164(1A) deals with the size of the Council of Ministers.

s: Who among the following became Deputy Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh in the government formed in 2024?
x: K. Pawan Kalyan of the Jana Sena is the Deputy Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh (2026).

s: The reported 2026 proposal for automatic removal of the Prime Minister, Chief Minister or a Minister concerns detention for
o: 30 consecutive days on charges carrying five or more years of imprisonment
60 consecutive days on charges carrying ten or more years of imprisonment
x: The 130th Constitutional Amendment Bill proposes automatic removal after detention for 30 consecutive days on charges carrying a possible sentence of five or more years.

s: Under the Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, 2025, on which day is a PM, CM or Minister in custody for 30 consecutive days for an offence punishable with five years or more removed?
x: The Bill (amending Articles 75, 164 and 239AA) provides removal on the 31st day after 30 consecutive days in custody.

s: Which Articles does the Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, 2025 propose to amend?
x: The Bill amends Articles 75, 164 and 239AA to remove a PM, CM or Minister held in custody for 30 consecutive days.

s: Under which Article is the Advocate General of a State appointed?
x: Article 165 provides for the Advocate General, the State counterpart of the Attorney General (Art. 76).

s: Who determines the remuneration of the Advocate General of a State?
x: The Governor appoints the Advocate General and determines his remuneration, not the Legislature.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Advocate General of a State:
1. He holds office during the pleasure of the Governor.
2. He has the right to vote in the State Legislature under Article 177.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct. Under Article 177 he may speak and take part in proceedings but has no vote.

s: A person to be appointed Advocate General of a State must be qualified to be appointed as which of the following?
x: The Advocate General must be qualified to be a High Court judge: a citizen with 10 years of judicial office or as an HC advocate.
